chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansur, from Alaa ibn Rab' (or Abdul-Alla), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A man's intellect is considered/measured by three things: in the length of his beard, in the engraving of his ring, and in his kunya (nickname).

key_terms.كُنْيَتِهِ: His kunya (nickname derived from father's name or child's name)

ai.seo_question: What three things measure a man's intellect according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking outward dignity—manifested through beard length, ring seal, and kunya—to inner intellectual discernment (*aql*). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *zahir* (external appearance) as a mirror of *batin* (internal state), where modesty and social identity serve as indicators of a person's maturity and wisdom.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-60 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Sahl ibn Zyad, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, on the authority of Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, on the authority of Abdul Ali - the servant of the Sam Clan - that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
One’s intellect can be measured by three things: long beard, marking on his ring and nickname.”
